sections.heading: Avatar
paragraphs: An avatar represents a user or entity with an image, an icon or initials, optionally paired with a name and email.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Avatars represent people and entities at a glance. Use AvatarGlyph on its own, or AvatarIdentity to pair it with a name, email and optional trailing icon.

sections.heading: Components
paragraphs: An AvatarGlyph with name, optional email and optional trailing icon.
The avatar alone — image, icon or initials.

sections.heading: Content types
paragraphs: For system or bot accounts, placeholders and entities that aren't people.
Initials — first letter of the first and last name.

sections.heading: When to use
paragraphs: •   To represent a person with their photo or initials.
•   To represent a system account, bot or non-person entity — Icon type.
•   To identify someone next to their name and email — AvatarIdentity.

sections.heading: Anatomy
paragraphs: •   ① Avatar — an AvatarGlyph instance (image, icon or initials).
•   ② Name — the person's or entity's name (Has name, Name).
•   ③ Email (optional) — secondary line (Has email, Email).
•   ④ Trailing icon (optional) — e.g. a chevron for a menu (Has trailing icon).

sections.heading: Colors
paragraphs: Derive an initials avatar's color from a hash of the user's name or ID, so the same person always gets the same color.
The same person gets the same color everywhere.
Don't assign a random color on each render.

sections.heading: Main elements
paragraphs: •   First letter of the first and last name — Jane Doe → JD.
•   If the initials don't fit, shrink the font to fit rather than clip.
•   Needs alt text that names the person.
•   If the image fails to load, fall back to the icon (if configured), then to initials.
•   Set with the Name and Email text properties.

sections.heading: States
paragraphs: AvatarGlyph is static. AvatarIdentity has interactive states for when it opens a profile card or menu.
See the Style tab for how each state looks.

sections.heading: Interactions
paragraphs: An avatar that opens a profile card or menu needs hover and focus states like a button. A purely decorative avatar has no hover styling, so it doesn't look clickable.
Moves focus to an interactive AvatarIdentity

sections.heading: Related
paragraphs: •   Badge — overlay a Dot or Numeric badge on an avatar for notifications. Keep it distinct from a presence/status dot, which signals identity state rather than action required.

sections.heading: What the design system provides
paragraphs: •   A Focused state with a 3px ring on AvatarIdentity.
•   Hover, Active, Selected and Disabled states for interactive avatars.
•   Sizes of 24, 32 and 40px — the smallest meets the 24×24px AA target minimum (WCAG 2.5.8).

sections.heading: Development considerations
paragraphs: •   Image avatars need alt text that names the person — not "avatar" or "user photo".
•   Icon and initials avatars need an accessible name (aria-label); two letters alone aren't enough context.
•   Announce a numbered notification badge as part of the name — e.g. "Jane Doe, 3 notifications".
•   Interactive avatars need hover and focus states like a button; decorative avatars have none.
•   An overflow "+N" avatar in a group must reveal the remaining names with a keyboard-triggerable popover, not hover only.

sections.heading: Keyboard interactions
paragraphs: Moves focus to an interactive AvatarIdentity
Moves focus to the previous focusable element

sections.heading: Design recommendations
paragraphs: Automated contrast check — WCAG 2.x relative luminance (sRGB), for every theme combination. Initials (12px) and name/email text need 4.5:1; icons and the focus ring 3:1; disabled text 3:1 (house rule TKN-005). Note: project-a / light is measured against the current surface/bg/default, which resolves to blue because of the gray/50 token.
